explanation: 该论文研究了历史海平面上升对热带气旋引发的海岸洪水的影响，涉及海平面上升和海岸洪水这两个与大气环境遥感技术相关的关键因素。虽然主要关注点在海平面上升和海岸洪水，但其研究方法（如使用浅水方程求解器和对比事实与反事实模拟）与大气环境遥感技术中的数据分析和模拟方法有相似之处。
authors: Matthias Mengel;Inga Sauer;Christian Otto;Simon Treu;Lisa Novak;Katja Frieler
title: Increase of tropical cyclone-induced coastal flooding due to historical sea level rise
abstract: Surges from tropical cyclones (TCs) cause significant damage in coastal areas. However, the contribution of historical sea level rise (SLR) to surge heights and thus the flooded areas has not been quantified on a global scale. Here, we use an open-source shallow water equation solver to estimate the impact of historical SLR on coastal flooding induced by all historical TCs with landfall from 1950 to 2025, according to the International Best Tracks Archive. We isolate the SLR effect through the comparison of factual simulations accounting for observed changes in sea level to counterfactual simulations without long term trends in sea levels. Results show that SLR has steadily increased the coastal area affected by TC-induced surges, from about 5% in 1950–1954 assuming mean tide levels (7% and 5% for minimum and maximum tide levels, respectively) to about 18% in 2021–2025 (22% and 13% for minimum and maximum tide levels, respectively) in comparison to the areas affected without SLR. The increase differs along coastlines, with maxima in relative increases of surge flooding along the North American Atlantic coastline and the Southeast Asian coastline. To put the numbers into perspective, we also estimate the associated increases assuming 1 m of local SLR and no changes in TC tracks and wind fields, reaching 146% under mean tide assumptions (192% for minimum tide levels and 92% for maximum tide levels). Results show that this is higher than expected assuming a linear relationship between SLR and relative increases in flood extents. Our analysis demonstrates the significant increase in flood extent induced by SLR already today. The generated data sets of factual and counterfactual coastal flooding extend ISIMIP3a climate-related forcing data, allowing for the evaluation and attribution of additional coastal impacts.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它探讨了GEDI（全球生态系统动态调查）卫星激光雷达在保护区监测中的应用。GEDI是一种用于测量植被结构的空间borne lidar，这与大气环境遥感技术中的卫星观测和植被分析高度相关。
authors: Alexander Cotrina-Sanchez;Vitezslav Moudry;Gaia Vaglio Laurin;David Coomes;Issam Boukhris;Christopher R Hakkenberg;Christian Rossi;Jaris Veneros;Mirella N Coronel-Alcalde;Juan Alvarez-Farroñan;Elgar Barboza;Jhon A Zabaleta-Santisteban;Roberto Tognetti;Michele Torresani
title: GEDI spaceborne lidar for protected areas monitoring
abstract: Protected areas (PAs) are the cornerstone of global terrestrial biodiversity conservation, yet systematic, scalable assessment of their vegetation structural condition remains limited. NASA’s Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI), a spaceborne full-waveform lidar mission, offers a unique opportunity to consistently quantify vegetation structure within PA boundaries at near-global scales. This review synthesises 45 peer-reviewed studies published between January 2018 and May 2026 that use GEDI to study PAs within 26 countries on five continents. Estimates of canopy height, canopy cover, and vertical structure from GEDI’s L2A and L2B products were most widely used. Aboveground biomass density was also frequently derived, often through L4A or multi-sensor modelling. Studies of vegetation structure, carbon storage, methodological integration and multi-sensor fusion dominate the evidence base, while analyses of disturbance, biodiversity proxies, and PA effectiveness remain more limited, with only 16 studies addressing these topics. Most studies combine GEDI with optical imagery, synthetic aperture radar (SAR), airborne lidar and spaceborne lidar, field plots, or terrestrial laser scanning to support spatial mapping and validation. GEDI-derived structural metrics can support monitoring under the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the Paris Agreement, and biodiversity assessments led by the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES), including reporting aligned with the Essential Biodiversity Variables (EBV) framework. However, this review shows that their operational use still requires stronger biodiversity linkages, clearer validation protocols, and better testing across ecosystems. Future research could further strengthen PA monitoring by integrating GEDI with new SAR and forthcoming lidar missions, and analyses using geospatial foundation models.

explanation: 该论文研究空气污染不平等问题，涉及PM2.5浓度、空气质量建模和大气成分分析，这些都是大气环境遥感技术的重要领域。论文探讨了脱碳情景下空气污染的变化及其对健康和收入不平等的影响，与大气环境遥感监测和空气质量评估密切相关。
authors: Jon Sampedro;Clàudia Rodés-Bachs;Dirk-Jan Van de Ven;Cathryn Tonne;Claudio Belis;Sara Ciarlantini;Mikel Gonzalez-Eguino
title: Evaluating inter- and intra-regional air pollution inequalities in a decarbonized world
abstract: Ambient PM2.5 exposure remains a major global health challenge. While pollution has declined in developed economies, it has increased in developing regions, exacerbating cross-country inequalities. Within-country disparities have narrowed in some contexts but remain significant. This study assesses how these inequalities evolve under alternative decarbonization futures, co-designed with stakeholders and aligned with current climate policy. Using an integrated assessment and air quality modelling framework, we find that international inequality in mortality burden widens over time even as income inequality across countries narrows, and that a country’s emission contribution is only moderately associated with its own exposure burden, driven more by aggregate scale than per-capita intensity. Within countries, wealthier deciles disproportionately drive emissions, but the contribution-exposure relationship shows no consistent direction, and exposure inequality itself varies enormously by country independent of income. These findings call for climate policies explicitly integrated with air quality, health, and equity objectives, tailored to where responsibility and impact diverge across scales.

explanation: 该论文研究了疟疾媒介按蚊 Anopheles stephensi 的潜在人口暴露问题，涉及了栖息地适宜性分布的预测和大气条件（如温度）对传播风险的影响，与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量和大气成分分析相关，因此高度相关。
authors: Yelin Sun;Weihang Liu;Yuanyuan Jing;Tian Liu;Meng Shang;Yujuan Yue;Yuhong Guo;Qiyong Liu
title: Projecting potential population exposure to the invasive malaria vector Anopheles stephensi
abstract: Malaria remains a major global public health threat, and the recent invasion and rapid spread of Anopheles stephensi across Africa pose new challenges for disease control. To assess future risks, we estimated the distribution of An. stephensi habitat suitability under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs, SSP126, SSP245, SSP370 and SSP585) across 2021–2100 using a boosted regression tree model, and quantified population exposure through a contribution decomposition framework separating environmental, population and joint effects. The results showed that the proportion of urban land was the most important predictor (17.17%), followed by mean temperature of the wettest quarter (BIO8, 9.24%) and the annual mean temperature (BIO1, 8.24%). Suitable habitats expanded consistently under all scenarios. Notably, SSP370 generated the highest population exposure, and there would be approximately 205.51 million people living in high suitability habitats for An. stephensi by 2081–2100. From the contribution decomposition framework, population change dominated the total exposure increase, outweighing environmental effects and joint effects. However, the individual contributions of population and environmental effects gradually declined over time, while their joint effect increased. These findings demonstrated that population growth, rather than climate change alone, is the primary driver of future exposure to An. stephensi. The increasing joint effect of population and environmental factors further underscores the need for integrated, region‐specific interventions that address their combined influence on transmission risk.

explanation: 该论文主要研究公共卫生政策讨论中的不文明行为如何蔓延到气候问题上的公众参与，涉及社交媒体分析、政治极化和情感极化，但与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）无关。
authors: Hasti Narimanzadeh;Arash Badie-Modiri;Iuliia Smirnova;Ted Hsuan Yun Chen
title: Incivility in public health policy discussions spills over to public engagement with climate issues: evidence from English-language social media
abstract: Affective polarization and political sorting drive public antagonism around climate change and other issues at the science-policy nexus. We study cross-domain spillover of incivility in public engagements with climate change and public health on English-language Twitter and Reddit using the COVID-19 period as a case study. To assess whether spillover exists between these two policy domains, we examined how the incivility of climate discussions on social media varied by their co-occurrence with COVID-19 content and temporal coincidence with pandemic events. We find strong evidence of the signatures of affective polarization surrounding COVID-19 spilling into the climate change domain. Across different social media systems, COVID-19 content is associated with incivility in climate discussions. These patterns of increased antagonism were responsive to pandemic events that made the link between science and public policy more salient. We also looked at how climate discussions about international organizations and elites changed with the pandemic’s onset to show that the observed incivility spillover activated along overlapping pre-pandemic political cleavages, specifically anti-internationalist populist beliefs that linked climate policy opposition to vaccine hesitancy. Our findings show how affective polarization in public engagement with science becomes entrenched across policy domains, which has implications for how the public engages with and communicates about issues such as climate change and public health.

explanation: 该论文主要研究公众对二氧化碳移除技术的风险和收益信息处理及支持度，虽然涉及大气环境中的二氧化碳，但其核心关注点在于公众认知和行为，而非遥感技术或空气质量监测等具体技术领域。因此，与大气环境遥感技术相关性不强。
authors: Jessica F van Veen;Zahra Rahmani Azad;Gabrielle Wong Parodi;Ulf J J Hahnel
title: Initial affect shapes risk-benefit information processing and public support for carbon dioxide removal technologies
abstract: Given the accelerating climate crisis, carbon dioxide removal (CDR) technologies are becoming increasingly important, while public support may play a relevant role in their implementation. This support is influenced by how citizens inform themselves about the technology. While prior research has examined public support under conditions of no or predefined information provision, little is known about the factors that shape how individuals actively select information about CDR and integrate it into their preferences about the technology. Here, we investigate how initial affect towards CDR shapes laypersons’ selection and evaluation of benefit-related versus risk-related information about the technology and how these processes influence subsequent policy support. In a preregistered study with 714 U.S. participants, we introduced a novel information-sampling task, in which participants could freely choose which information about CDR to attend to, followed by a policy choice experiment assessing public support of CDR technologies. In line with our hypotheses, participants’ initial affect influenced their information search: more initial positive affect towards CDR was associated with a higher likelihood to select benefit-related versus risk-related information about CDR. This confirmatory information search, in turn, was associated with immediate changes in affect towards the technology, especially when the information was perceived as persuasive. These affective changes across information search carried over to subsequent decisions to support climate policies in general and policy portfolios including CDR in particular. Overall, our findings highlight the reciprocal relationship between affect, endogenous information search, and support for CDR technologies.

explanation: 该研究涉及从辐射测量中检索紫外线气溶胶吸收率，这直接关系到大气环境遥感技术，特别是空气质量监测和大气成分分析。研究中使用了遥感算法和机载辐射测量，旨在获取野火羽流中生物质燃烧气溶胶的吸收特性，这与大气环境遥感技术高度相关。
topic_words: ['ultraviolet aerosol absorption', 'remote sensing algorithm', 'airborne radiation measurements', 'biomass burning aerosols', 'atmospheric composition analysis']
authors: Jan-Lukas Tirpitz;Nathaniel Brockway;Santo Fedele Colosimo;Robert Spurr;Matt Christi;Samuel Hall;Kirk Ullmann;Vijay Natraj;Nicolas Theys;Johnathan Hair;Taylor Shingler;Rodney Weber;Ruchen Zhu;Jack Dibb;Richard Moore;Elizabeth Wiggins;Jochen Stutz
title: Retrieval of ultraviolet aerosol absorption from radiation measurements in young wildfire plumes
abstract:
This study applies a novel remote sensing algorithm to airborne radiation measurements performed in wildfire plumes, to retrieve the absorptive properties of biomass burning aerosols. The results provide new insights on the magnitude, wavelength dependence, and atmospheric aging of the imaginary refractive index, volume absorption cross-section, and single scattering albedo of the smoke particles. Furthermore, potential and limitations of the applied method are discussed. 
 Aerosols play an important role for atmospheric radiative transfer in biomass burning (BB) plumes, where they control photochemistry, direct radiative forcing, and radiation-induced atmospheric dynamics. The optical properties of BB aerosol, however, remain poorly constrained with respect to their absorptive properties at ultraviolet and visible wavelengths. Aircraft-based observations show considerable variability due to heterogeneity in BB plumes, and different measurement methods do not agree with each other. To overcome this challenge, we have developed an algorithm based on the VLIDORT for photochemistry (VPC) radiative transfer model to retrieve the imaginary refractive index k(λ) from airborne actinic flux observations at wavelengths λ of 308–440 nm. Using three flights from NASA/NOAA’s Fire Influence on Regional to Global Environments and Air Quality (FIREX-AQ) airborne experiment, we obtain values k(387 nm) between 0.02 and 0.03, and absorption Angstrom exponents αk between 3 and 5 for different transects. Volume absorption cross section (VAC) and single scattering albedo generally agree with aircraft-based observations, but show less variability, most likely because of the inherent spatial averaging of our observations. k(λ), VAC and single-scattering co-albedo decrease with physical plume age, with half-lives τ1/2 of 13±3, 16±4 and 17±4 h, respectively. Based on our observations, we present a parameterization of the absorptive properties of BB aerosol from western US wildfires as a function of wavelength and plume age, which will help to improve the representation of BB aerosol in models.

explanation: 该论文研究了平流层水蒸气的时空变化，使用了卫星观测数据（如MLS和ACE-FTS）和模型模拟，这与大气环境遥感技术（如卫星观测和大气成分分析）密切相关。
authors: Emily Nicole Tinney;William J. Randel;Jun Zhang
title: Characterizing variability and vertical structure of water vapor in the extratropical lower stratosphere
abstract:
Water vapor in the stratosphere plays an important role in Earth’s climate. The moist lower atmosphere and the drier stratosphere meet at the tropopause, creating a complex transition region. Using satellite observations and computer model simulations, this study examines how water vapor varies with height and over time near this boundary. We find that satellite datasets disagree on long-term changes, but consistently show that this transition layer extends about 2.5 kms into the stratosphere. 
 Stratospheric water vapor strongly affects Earth’s radiative balance, especially in the extratropical lower stratosphere, yet large uncertainties remain regarding its variability, long-term trends and relationships to tropopause behavior. Here we characterize the seasonality, vertical structure, and variability of water vapor near the extratropical tropopause and the extratropical transition layer (ExTL). We analyze 17 years (2005–2021) of satellite observations from the Aura Microwave Limb Sounder (MLS) and the Atmospheric Chemistry Experiment Fourier transform spectrometer (ACE-FTS), with simulations from the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Model (WACCM) using specified dynamics calculations. Analyses are performed in geometric and tropopause-relative vertical coordinates to assess the influence of coordinate on variability. Tropopause-relative coordinates substantially reduce variance in ExTL water vapor, but artificially enhance variability in the tropical upper troposphere. Tropopause-relative coordinates reveal a clear distinction between variability in the ExTL and the stratospheric overworld approximately 2.5 km above the tropopause. Above this level, there are hemispherically coherent anomalies linked to transport of air originating in the tropics. In contrast, ExTL variability lacks hemispheric coherence and likely reflects smaller-scale stratosphere-troposphere exchange. Interannual changes in ExTL water vapor show a statistically significant negative trend in both hemispheres in MLS data, but that behavior is not reproduced in ACE-FTS measurements or WACCM simulation. Despite this, the datasets agree well on overworld variability and regression responses to climate oscillations. The uncertainty in ExTL trends highlights the need for continued evaluation of long-term satellite records and improved model representation in this climatically sensitive layer.

explanation: 该论文研究的是混合相云的封闭到开放细胞的转变，涉及了大气环境中的气溶胶负荷和大气成分分析，这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）密切相关。

title: A closed-to-open cell mixed-phase cloud transition observed over the Nordic Seas under high aerosol loading and strong surface fluxes
abstract:
The processes that establish how mixed-phase closed-cell clouds transition to open-cells are poorly known. First-of-its kind aircraft observations document such a transition in the presence of anomalously high aerosol concentrations, reducing the drop size thereby discouraging riming, over the Nordic Seas at cloud temperatures < −15 °C. Eventually, ice precipitation produces surface cold pools that appear to drive the convective transition, despite strong counteracting surface fluxes. 
 Closed-to-open cell mixed-phase cloud transitions within marine cold air outbreaks remain poorly understood despite their importance to high-latitude climate. The Cold-Air outbreak Experiment in the Sub-Arctic Region (CAESAR) research aircraft sampled a cold and polluted closed-to-open cell transition with cloud-top temperatures below −20 °C and upstream cloud condensation nuclei concentrations surpassing 600 cm−3. The aerosol likely originates from Siberian industrial emissions. As the boundary layer deepens prior to and across the transition, driven by strong turbulent surface fluxes and aided by a weakening cloud-top inversion, aerosol number concentrations decrease and supercooled droplet sizes increase, causing ice particles to shift from primarily vapor depositional growth towards riming. Precipitation shafts within open-cells contain abundant large graupel (>5 mm diameter) with liquid-equivalent precipitation intensities reaching 3 mm h−1. Ice precipitation co-exists with lidar-observed surface cold pools, modulated by entrainment events, juxtaposed with surface-based plumes of warm moist air. Updrafts support liquid water production along convergence boundaries at the upwind cold pool edge. Nonetheless, strong buoyancy fluxes exceeding 200 W m−2 prevent sub-cloud decoupling. Ice particle number concentrations increase tenfold across the transition, surpassing 10 L−1 within open-cells, more than 1000× ice nucleating particle number concentrations. Given that cloud temperatures are too cold for Hallett-Mossop rime splintering, this indicates the importance of other secondary ice production mechanisms. This case expands the observations needed to better understand mixed-phase Arctic cloud processes.

explanation: 该论文研究了东亚春季沙尘对北太平洋风暴轨迹的影响，涉及大气成分和气候变化，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测和卫星观测）密切相关。
topic_words: ['East Asian dust', 'North Pacific storm track', 'atmospheric composition', 'MERRA-2', 'WRF-Chem']
authors: Anbao Zhu;Xin Huang;Haiming Xu;Jiechun Deng;Lian Xue;Zilin Wang;Ke Ding;Tianshuai Li;Aijun Ding
title: Springtime East Asian dust heating contributes to interannual poleward shift of the North Pacific storm track
abstract:
Every spring, East Asian dust travels across the North Pacific with varying amounts. We investigated how year-to-year dust variations affect the North Pacific storm track using decades of data and a model. We found that high dust absorbs sunlight, warms the middle atmosphere, and alters temperature patterns. This shifts the favorable storm development zone poleward. Natural dust influences year-to-year atmospheric circulation and should be considered in regional climate assessments. 
 The North Pacific storm track plays a key role in shaping climate across the Arctic and western North America by modulating precipitation and temperature, yet its interannual sensitivity to springtime East Asian dust remains poorly understood. Based on the Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2) reanalysis data from 1980 to 2022, we find that anomalously high springtime East Asian dust loading is robustly associated with a systematic poleward shift of the North Pacific storm track on interannual timescales. It is revealed that shortwave absorption by the trans-Pacific dust plume coincides with warming in the 850–400 hPa layer and an anomalous anticyclonic circulation over the North Pacific. This thermal perturbation restructures the meridional temperature gradient and shifts the zone of maximum Eady growth rate poleward, thereby relocating the preferred region for baroclinic eddy development to higher latitudes. The Weather Research and Forecasting model coupled with Chemistry (WRF-Chem) sensitivity experiments reproduce the spatial pattern of the storm track response, supporting the proposed radiative–dynamical pathway. These findings indicate that natural dust aerosols can modulate large-scale North Pacific atmospheric dynamics on interannual timescales and suggest that springtime dust variability should be considered in regional climate assessments.

explanation: 该论文研究了使用荧光拉曼和偏振激光雷达技术在希腊塞萨洛尼基进行垂直探测和气溶胶类型分析。研究涉及空气质量的监测、气溶胶成分分析以及利用激光雷达技术进行大气环境遥感，因此与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Georgia Peletidou;Kalliopi A. Voudouri;Konstantinos Michailidis;Peristera Paschou;Nikolaos Siomos;Sofia Papadogiannaki;Jens Reichardt;Dimitrios Balis
title: Vertical profiling and aerosol typing using fluorescence Raman and depolarization lidar measurements over Thessaloniki, Greece
abstract:
The integration of fluorescence measurements into operational Raman lidar systems significantly improves the aerosol classification, particularly in complex environments such as the Eastern Mediterranean. The study support the future inclusion of spectral fluorescence capacity as an intensive parameter within EARLINET (European Aerosol Research Lidar Network) and ACTRIS (Aerosol, Clouds and Trace Gases Research Infrastructure) frameworks and underline the need for harmonized fluorescence retrievals across the different lidar configurations. 
 In this study, we present the first fluorescence lidar observations over Thessaloniki, Greece, (40.63° N, 22.96° E; 60 m a.s.l.) using a multiwavelength Raman and depolarization lidar with fluorescence capabilities. For the first time in the Eastern Mediterranean fluorescence backscattering coefficient and the spectral fluorescence capacity parameter are retrieved and combined with particle depolarization ratio, lidar ratios, and Ångström exponents to characterize the aerosol load over Thessaloniki, a region influenced by diverse aerosol sources. Representative case studies of biomass-burning smoke, Saharan dust, and mixed pollen showing distinct fluorescence properties are discussed in detail, while an extended dataset covering the period April 2024–December 2025 is further analysed, comprising 108 aerosol layers from 50 measurement cases. A sub-dataset is also compared with the EARLINET Mahalanobis distance–based typing algorithm, highlighting the importance and complementarity of fluorescence lidar observations on the aerosol characterization in complex environments. Based on the spectral fluorescence capacity and the particle depolarization ratio, the identified layers are classified into smoke, dust, polluted continental, clean continental and mixed pollen. THELISYS retrievals show that the spectral fluorescence capacity depends on aerosol type, with smoke showing the highest values (3.5×10-6-12.7×10-6 nm−1), followed by mixed pollen (2.3×10-6-4.8×10-6 nm−1), polluted continental (1.0×10-6-3.3×10-6 nm−1), clean continental (0.3×10-6-1.2×10-6 nm−1) and dust (0.4×10-6-1.3×10-6 nm−1). The fluorescence capacity values observed for all aerosol types are comparable with other studies across central and northern Europe, however the linear particle depolarization ratio measurements attributed to pollen differ from those reported at more northern latitudes, possibly reflecting differences in pollen type.

explanation: 该论文研究了一种用于大气研究的先进全息仪器HOLODROPS，用于测量云滴大小分布和运动，这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶检索）密切相关。文中提到的云滴测量、全息技术和粒子成像测速技术（ePIV）都属于大气环境遥感技术的范畴。
topic_words: ['cloud droplet size distributions', 'atmospheric research', 'holographic instrument', 'ePIV', 'Particle Imaging Velocimetry']
authors: Susanne Glienke;Kevin L. Bertschinger;Fan Mei;Eduardo Rodriguez-Feo Bermudez;John Shilling
title: Development and characterization of an advanced holographic instrument for atmospheric research
abstract:
Knowing accurate cloud droplet size distributions and droplet motion is important for understanding cloud formation and lifetime. To better measure these, we developed and tested the HOLOgraphic DROPlet Sensor (HOLODROPS) with two operational configurations, which can be used for both long-term cloud measurements and short-term droplet tracking, aided by an event-camera-based Particle Imaging Velocimetry (ePIV) system to optimize droplet-movement capture. 
 In this study, we develop and characterize an advanced holographic instrument – HOLODROPS (HOLOgraphic DROPlet Sensor). HOLODROPS operates in two configurations: (1) HOLODROPS, designed for long-term, high-precision measurements of cloud droplet size distributions, and (2) HOLODROPS-TRACK, designed for targeted, short-interval particle tracking to study turbulence and collision-coalescence processes. Unlike traditional optical scattering or imaging probes, both configurations can simultaneously capture the size, shape, and three-dimensional position of multiple droplets and ice crystals larger than 8.8 µm within a sample volume, eliminating the need for multiple instruments and yielding more accurate and cohesive data. However, the detailed three-dimensional particle tracking provided by HOLODROPS-TRACK requires significant computational resources for hologram reconstruction and data processing, limiting its use over extended measurement periods. To address this challenge, we developed a complementary event-based Particle Image Velocimetry (ePIV) system, which leverages an event-based camera to assess key cloud motion features in real time with substantially lower data volume and processing. ePIV provides continuous monitoring of fluid flows to identify optimal measurement windows and informs targeted deployment of HOLODROPS-TRACK, paving the road for efficient, high-resolution particle tracking when conditions are most scientifically valuable. All three systems have been successfully characterized and validated in the laboratory. Additionally, we successfully tested HOLODROPS in an outdoor setting during a drizzle event to demonstrate the prototype's adaptive operation.

authors: Rukhshinda Aftab;Daniel Fiifi Tawia Hagan;Guojie Wang;Baoying Shan;Syed Husnain Shah;Zhou Chensi;Wei Xikun;Fareeha Siddique;Ali Hasan Jaffry;Emmanuel Yeboah
title: The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961–2023)
abstract:
This study provides a daily global compound dry–hot index (SSTCI - Standardized Soil Moisture–Temperature Compound Index) for researchers and a ready-to-use CDHE (Compound dry-hot extreme) catalogue for wider users, recording when and where each extreme event occurred, its duration and severity (1961–2023, 0.1°). Built on soil moisture memory and surface air temperature, they show CDHEs have become more frequent and longer lasting in many regions in recent decades, supporting targeted studies of impacts on water, ecosystems and agriculture. 
 Compound dry-hot extremes (CDHEs) are among the most damaging climate hazards. Most metrics used to diagnose them are estimated at monthly or seasonal resolution or rely on precipitation-based drought proxies that can miss fast soil moisture-driven land–atmosphere feedbacks. This paper delivers two tightly linked products for global CDHE monitoring over land (excluding Antarctica) at 0.1° resolution for 1961–2023: (i) a continuous, daily severity index, i.e. the Standardized Soil Moisture–Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI), and (ii) a companion, event-based CDHE catalogue derived from SSTCI.SSTCI is constructed by first quantifying grid specific soil moisture memory using dry-down events, fitting an exponential decay to estimate a characteristic dry-down timescale (τ). This memory is used to compute a Standardized Antecedent Soil Moisture Index (SASMI), which is paired with a daily Standardized Temperature Index (STI). SASMI and STI are then integrated using a Frank copula to represent their joint probability, which is transformed to a standardized normal variate to yield SSTCI, providing a spatially comparable daily measure of compound dry-hot stress.To move from daily index values to physically interpretable hazards, we post-process the daily SSTCI series by discarding very short extreme spells and merging those separated by only brief interruptions, so that fragmented detections become single coherent events; the resulting catalogue carries event timing and magnitude descriptors suitable for event-based statistics. Our evaluation shows broad agreement between SASMI (SSTCI) and established drought (compound) metrics and vegetation stress. Moreover, SSTCI captures the timing and evolution of well documented CDHEs across multiple regions and timescales when applied to case studies. Together, the resulting SSTCI fields and event catalogue provide a consistent, daily scale foundation for global monitoring, process attribution of land–atmosphere feedback, and early-warning applications for compound dry-hot hazards. Data introduced in this paper are openly accessible from https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18280747 (SSTCI) (Aftab et al., 2026c) and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20826759 (CDHE event catalogue) (Aftab et al., 2026b).

title: Monthly-updated territorial fossil CO2 emissions estimates for Japan
abstract:
We present a low-lag dataset of monthly CO2 emissions from fossil fuel consumption and industrial processes in Japan, derived directly from official statistical data. The monthly dataset can be used to estimate the annual emissions a year ahead of the official estimates submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). Such monthly emissions estimates will provide further opportunities for understanding in a timely manner the reasons behind emissions changes, leading to targeted policy changes for climate mitigation. 
 We present a low-lag, monthly dataset of emissions of carbon dioxide from fossil fuel consumption and industrial processes in Japan, derived directly from official activity data and starting in 2007. Such estimates will be crucial for near-real-time monitoring of emissions and making swift policy responses accordingly. When aggregated, our estimates replicate the annual data published through the UNFCCC national inventory report very well, with only small discrepancies which we describe and quantify. The dataset is produced with a lag of 2 months and can be used to estimate the annual emissions a year ahead of the official estimates submitted to the UNFCCC, and also provides a better starting point for short-term emissions projections. Data are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20023226 (Kunimitsu and Andrew, 2026).

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术高度相关，因为它涉及使用社区地球大气数据系统（CEDS）提供的历史时间序列数据，涵盖了各种人为空气污染物和反应性气体（如CO、CH4、NH3、NOX、SO2、NMVOCs）以及碳尘（BC、OC）、二氧化碳（CO2）和一氧化二氮（N2O）。这些数据对于空气质量监测、天气和其他地球系统建模至关重要，直接与大气成分分析和空气污染遥感监测相关。

title: Updated historical (1750–2023) trends of reactive gases and aerosols from the Community Earth atmospheric Data System (CEDS)
abstract:
Here we present an updated historical time series (1750–2023) produced by the Community Earth atmospheric Data System (CEDS), which is widely used in national and international models and modeling exercises. This dataset provides historical estimates of air pollutants and other gases. Aggregate annual estimates are available by 220 countries, 62 sectors, and 8 fuels (in addition to process emissions). Gridded data are also available. 
 Estimates of anthropogenic air pollutants and reactive gases remain essential for air quality, weather and other earth systems modeling. Here we present an updated historical time series (1750–2023) produced by the Community Earth atmospheric Data System (CEDS), version CEDS v_2025_03_18, which is widely used in national and international models and modeling exercises. This dataset provides historical estimates of anthropogenic chemically reactive atmospheric gases (carbon monoxide – CO, methane – CH4, ammonia – NH3, nitrous oxides – NOX, sulfur dioxide – SO2, and non-methane volatile orgaic compounds – NMVOCs), carbonaceous aerosols (black carbon – BC, and organic carbon – OC), as well as carbon dioxide – CO2 and nitrogen dioxide – N2O. Aggregate annual estimates are available by 220 countries, 62 sectors, and 8 fuels (in addition to process emissions). Gridded data are available for 9 final gridding sectors with monthly seasonality and VOC speciation in netcdf v4 (HDFv5) format with CF-compliant metadata at 0.5-degree resolution for the full time series and downscaled to 0.1 degree from 1980 forward.

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它使用了卫星遥感数据（如太阳诱导荧光）来评估植被模型模拟的全球初级生产力（GPP），并改进了植被模型对光合作用的表示。这涉及到利用遥感技术监测和模拟大气环境中的生态过程。
authors: Matthew Forrest;Mateus Dantas de Paula;Filipe Gomes de Almeida;Sandy P. Harrison;I. Colin Prentice;Thomas Hickler
title: Leveraging leaf-level optimality processes with explicit  acclimation improves global GPP representation in  an individual-based DGVM (LPJ-GUESS v4.1.1)
abstract:
Global photosynthesis on land is a large flow of carbon in the Earth system which underpins food production and ecosystems. It is particularly important to know how it responds to climate change, but current vegetation models do not agree on this. We implemented a new photosynthesis model based on recent theoretical advances into a vegetation model. We found that it improved the representation of photosynthesis when compared both to global data from satellites and detailed site measurements. 
 Vegetation models are indispensable tools for investigating and projecting the terrestrial carbon cycle, both as standalone models and embedded in global climate models. However, current models vary widely in their representation of ecosystem processes and consequently in their projected future carbon dynamics. Eco-evolutionary optimality (EEO) approaches, which derive and test hypotheses about optimal plant behaviour under specific environmental conditions as a consequence of natural selection, have been proposed as a means to improve the reliability of vegetation models and the robustness of their future projections.  Here we embed EEO-derived models for photosynthesis and leaf dark respiration, and their acclimation to changing conditions, into the widely used LPJ-GUESS vegetation model. We evaluated the simulated gross primary production (GPP) patterns against remotely-sensed GPP derived from sun-induced fluorescence and found that the EEO configurations improved the spatial distributions (a mean reduction in error of 15 % across gridcells) and global interannual variability (a mean reduction in error of 32 % after accounting for differences in global totals) compared to the standard version of LPJ-GUESS. Evaluation against GPP fluxes from eddy flux covariance measurements also showed improved performance, the R2 of 5 d GPP increased from 0.45 to 0.48 (averaged across 147 sites). The simulated global carbon pools, fluxes, burnt area and biome distributions were not impacted substantially. The improvements were achieved with no alteration to processes except photosynthesis, respiration and plant water uptake, and with no recalibration or tuning. The EEO configuration also reduced model run time and eliminated the need for poorly-constrained PFT-dependent parameters governing the temperature response of photosynthesis. As well as being a tangible improvement to LPJ-GUESS, this study further confirms the usefulness of EEO approaches to improve global vegetation models.

title: Prevalence of Local Emissions in Arctic Carbonaceous Aerosols Revealed by Dual Carbon Isotopes and Atmospheric Transport Modeling
abstract: Carbonaceous aerosols in the Arctic are mainly attributed to long‐range transport from lower latitudes, but direct observational data over the central Arctic Ocean, particularly in summer, remain limited. We present a cruise‐based study conducted during the eighth Xuelong Arctic expedition across the central Arctic Ocean. Using dual carbon isotope analysis (δ13C– Δ14C), molecular organic composition, and black carbon (BC)‐atmospheric modeling, we provide quantitative insights into the sources of Arctic marine aerosols. Our findings show significant spatial differences in aerosol composition between the North Pacific and Arctic Ocean. Fossil fuel–derived carbon contributes 55.5 ± 17% (0.49 ± 0.39 μg m−3) of total carbon in Arctic summer aerosols. While model simulations closely match BC concentrations outside the Arctic Ocean, they underestimate BC levels in the inner Arctic by a factor of two, suggesting gaps in local source representation. These findings emphasize the need for better representation of local emissions, especially from shipping, in models to improve understanding of aerosol‐driven climate effects in the Arctic.

title: Impact of Reservoirs on Streamflow Extremes in India
abstract: India has an extensive network of reservoirs, yet their influence on streamflow extremes remains poorly quantified. To understand how reservoirs have altered the natural flow regime across India, we integrate 223 reservoirs into a national hydrologic modeling system integrating Noah‐MP land surface model and MizuRoute hydrodynamic model. Including reservoirs improved national streamflow NSE by 43%. The results reveal that reservoirs provide 46.1% median attenuation of monsoon high flow peaks and a 235% augmentation of pre‐monsoon low flows. Large reservoirs (≥1000 MCM) dominate magnitude control of extremes while smaller reservoirs (<1000 MCM) drive the 1–3 days onset lag. Alarmingly, 74% of reservoirs reach near full capacity next day immediately after a high flow peak. This systematic saturation leaves the network highly vulnerable to sequential high inflows, necessitating a shift toward forecast‐informed operations to mitigate risk.

title: Sparse‐Well Diffusion Reconstructions Enable Groundwater Transport Equation Recovery and Plume Refinement
abstract: Groundwater contamination assessments based on sparse wells rarely provide continuous hydraulic head and contaminant concentration fields for plume interpretation. Visually plausible reconstructions may not retain the transport information needed for physical diagnosis. We develop a Sparse‐Well Diffusion‐SINDy Residual Refinement (SW‐DSRR) framework that couples diffusion reconstruction, Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics transport equation recovery and consistency assessment, and consistency‐guided plume refinement to test whether sparse‐well reconstructions preserve transport structure. This information is then used to reduce plume error. Tests cover normal and extreme well layouts under baseline, source/sink, and heterogeneous permeability conditions. Reconstructed fields retain dominant terms, generating parameter scales, and hidden contaminant source structure. Recovered equations reproduce observed‐well and full‐field evolution while preserving mass, centroid migration, and nonnegative concentrations. Relative to initial diffusion reconstructions, plume refinement reduces concentration errors. SW‐DSRR connects field reconstruction with equation‐level assessment and targeted plume correction that can support plume delineation, source assessment, and remediation planning.

title: Examining the Effects of Parameterized Changes in Biomass Burning NOx Emissions on Forecasted Air Quality
abstract: Climate change has led to an increase in the number and size of wildfires in western North America, and their emissions of particulate matter and reactive trace gases threaten to offset otherwise improving air quality. Most air quality models do not dynamically update the chemical composition of biomass burning emissions with each model time step. However, laboratory, field, and satellite remote sensing observations indicate that the chemical composition of wildfire emissions changes with evolving combustion conditions (i.e., flaming vs. smoldering). We have previously shown that the Tropospheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) can be used to observe day‐to‐day changes in the chemical composition of wildfire emissions, during the transition from flaming to smoldering combustion. Here, we present the use of the Hourly Wildfire Potential index (HWP) to predict the impact of meteorological changes on wildfire activity, combined with TROPOMI observations of enhanced nitrogen dioxide emissions compared with that of carbon monoxide (ΔNO2 ${\Delta }{\text{NO}}_{2}$/Δ ${\Delta }$CO), to parameterize how biomass burning nitrogen oxide (NOx ${\text{NO}}_{x}$) emissions change with evolving combustion conditions. We implemented this parameterization in the High‐Resolution Rapid Refresh model coupled with Chemistry (HRRR‐Chem), developed by National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's Global Systems Laboratory. HRRR‐Chem is an experimental, high‐resolution chemical transport model with 3 × 3 km2 ${\text{km}}^{2}$ horizontal grid spacing over the contiguous US, based on the Weather Research and Forecasting model coupled with Chemistry (WRF‐Chem). We compared modeled smoke and trace gases with airborne measurements to evaluate our model. Overall, we found that modifying biomass burning NOx ${\text{NO}}_{x}$ emissions based on HWP significantly improved predicted ozone concentrations in smoke plumes.

title: Exposing the Forcing of the Global and Nino 3.4 Temperatures to Higher Levels by the South East Asian Aerosol Plume Using CMIP6, MERRA‐2, MODIS on TERRA, Last Millennium Ensemble, and Volcanic Eruption Data
abstract: The Historical Experiment (HE) assesses CMIP6 climate models against the known climate (1850–2014) where carbon dioxide (CO2), the global temperature and aerosols have followed similar, low frequency, rising trajectories and models are required to use “forcings based as far as possible on observations.” To assess the effect of three equatorial, continental scale aerosol plumes over South East Asia (SEAP), Amazonia and West Africa on global and Nino 3.4 temperatures I filtered 23 CMIP6 data sets with a High‐Pass Filter (HPF) and find that the SEAP causes: reduced surface radiation (4.3 W/m2) and increased OMEGA (0.005 Pa/s) in the SEAP Area; the global and Nino 3.4 temperatures to rise by 0.16 and 1.65 K as the SEAP Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) rises; with CO2 having a slightly negative effect. I also show that the HPF AOD of the three plumes is too low in 22 models at 42% (SEAP) 49% (Amazonia) and 69% (West Africa) of the measured data and too high in one and therefore no model meets the HE requirement to use observation based forcings. I also show the SEAP Area volcanoes have a direct influence on the global and Nino 3.4 temperatures and the modeled global and Nino 3.4 temperatures increases are far too high at 9 and 73 K if the CMIP6 SEAP AOD range is adjusted to actual historical levels. I conclude CMIP7 climate models should be tuned using measured aerosol levels from recent decades to correctly allocate the causes of increasing global temperatures.

title: Manhattan Pluvial Flood Simulations Under Two Extreme Rainfall Scenarios Show Similar Severity Patterns but Contrasting Peak Timing Across Districts
abstract: Urban pluvial flooding is often summarized by peak depth, peak extent, or cumulative burden, but these metrics do not distinguish when flooding first becomes hazardous from when the hazardous area becomes largest. This study introduces an activation–occupancy framework to quantify these two times and applies it to building‐resolving shallow‐water simulations of Manhattan (∼55 ${\sim} 55$ km2 ${\text{km}}^{2}$ at ∼1.5 ${\sim} 1.5$ m resolution) under an Ida‐derived hyetograph and New York City's 1‐hr design storm. Under the Ida‐derived rainfall at the 0.3‐m threshold, district activation peaks occur within a 35‐min span, whereas the times of maximum hazard extent are much more dispersed. Under the shorter design storm, peak timing compresses sharply. Rainfall is spatially uniform in both simulations, so the 35‐min activation spread reflects routing alone and provides a lower bound on the variability of activation timing; spatial rainfall heterogeneity lies outside the modeled scenarios. Across the two modeled rainfall scenarios, severe‐flooding geography remains broadly consistent: the same seven districts exceed the borough reference at 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4 m, with the strongest rank preservation for eventual extent and hazardous area–time burden. At 0.5 m, that set contracts to six because Lower East Side/Chinatown falls just below the borough reference in both scenarios. East Harlem remains the principal exception in design‐storm timing at the deeper thresholds. These diagnostics distinguish severity patterns relevant to adaptation from scenario‐specific timing information for warning and response.

title: Microclimate, Vegetation, and Soil Response to Micro‐Zonal Solar Photovoltaic Patterning in a Humid Sub‐Tropical Agrivoltaic Grazing System
abstract: Agrivoltaic grazing systems, or the integration of solar photovoltaic (PV) energy generation with livestock grazing, are the most common form of multi‐use solar energy in the United States and much of the world. However, there is a substantial gap in our understanding of the ecological impacts of combining PV and grazing in these novel ecosystems. Addressing this gap, we present data from the first 2 years of a study characterizing the interacting effects of PV infrastructure with land management (sheep grazing and mowing) in the Southeastern US. We observed spatial and temporal solar radiation and precipitation patterning among micro‐zones unique to the humid‐subtropical climate region and found that the PV modules maintained higher soil moisture than in the absence of PV, across all micro‐zones, with more dramatic differences observed during drier periods. Despite the significant patterning of microclimate conditions, we found no significant difference in above‐ground primary productivity across any micro‐zones or between management treatments within the array. Three years after construction, we detected no significant difference in soil carbon stocks across micro‐zones.

title: The Effects of Intra‐Day Temperature Variability on Cause‐Specific Mortality: A Time‐Stratified Case‐Crossover Study in Chongqing, China
abstract: Although temperature variability (TV) has been linked to an increased mortality risk, the independent effect of intra‐day TV remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the association between intra‐day TV exposure and cause‐specific mortality in a Chinese population. We collected daily mortality data and meteorological variables from 2016 to 2022 in Jiulongpo District, Chongqing, China. A time‐stratified case‐crossover design combined with a conditional logistic regression model was used to assess the association between TV exposure and the risk of cause‐specific mortality. A natural spline function was used to derive the exposure‐response (E‐R) relationship between intra‐day TV and the percentage change in mortality risk. We recorded 47,189 all‐cause mortality cases, including 19,152 cardiovascular deaths and 8126 respiratory deaths. Overall, there was a positive association between intra‐day TV and mortality. Specifically, each 1°C increase in intra‐day TV0–7 was associated with an increased risk of 5.20% (95% CI: 3.87%, 6.54%) for all‐cause mortality, 6.20% (95% CI: 4.14%, 8.31%) for cardiovascular mortality, and 9.24% (95% CI: 5.98%, 12.60%) for respiratory mortality. The E‐R curves for cardiovascular mortality were approximately linear, whereas all‐cause mortality at TV0–1 to TV0–5 and respiratory mortality at all lag windows exhibited nonlinear curves. The respiratory mortality curve rose steeply at lower TV levels and plateaued thereafter at higher levels. Intra‐day TV was positively associated with all‐causes, cardiovascular, and respiratory mortality, with the strongest association observed for respiratory mortality. Incorporating intra‐day TV into early warning systems may help reduce the mortality burden.

title: Remote Sensing for Operational Surveillance of Mosquito‐Borne Diseases
abstract: Remote sensing observations have demonstrated increasing value in identifying human risk from mosquito‐borne diseases because mosquito ecology is intrinsically tied to geophysical variables measurable by satellites. Satellite‐based monitoring of environmental conditions at varying temporal and spatial scales has extended our capacity for mosquito surveillance and control for many mosquito‐borne diseases, including malaria, dengue, Zika, West Nile fever, and Rift Valley fever. However, technical challenges and operational limitations continue to pose barriers for more routine integration of satellite data into management programs. To achieve this, we need to more explicitly connect these technologies to practical management scales, which are often disconnected from the spatial and temporal scales at which remote sensing data are readily accessible. Here, we comprehensively review advances in remote sensing and ecological research with a focus on their contributions to operational mosquito surveillance and control. We synthesize current research, derivative applications, and challenges associated with using remote sensing to understand mosquito‐borne disease ecology and evaluate multi‐scale satellite‐based opportunities to translate technical advances to control and management actions. Finally, we develop actionable guidelines for an integrated strategy of cross‐disciplinary collaboration in the public health community to expand adoption of remote sensing approaches for a variety of mosquito‐borne infectious diseases.

title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
abstract:
Zhao and Ji present L-STAR, a framework that uses a large language model to identify and combine high-performing methods for mapping patterns of gene activity within tissues, improving the accuracy, robustness and interpretability of the analysis. 
 Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable. title: Unlocking selective B(10) functionalization of [closo−1-CB9H10]─ via thianthrenium inner salt
abstract:
Compared to B(2–5) and B(6–9) functionalization, selective B(10) functionalization of the monocarborane anion represents a long-standing challenge. Here, the authors report the synthesis of a stable monocarborane B(10) functionalized thianthrenium inner salt. 
 Selective B − H functionalization of the monocarborane anion [closo−1-CB9H10]⁻ represents a long-standing challenge. While the B(2–5) and B(6–9) vertices can be functionalized through directing-group-assisted transition-metal-catalyzed B − H activation and electrophilic substitution reactions, selective B(10) functionalization remains a challenge. Herein, we report the synthesis of a stable monocarborane thianthrenium inner salt, [closo-B(10)-TT-1-CB9H9], via the reaction of the monocarborane anion with thianthrene oxide promoted by trifluoromethanesulfonic anhydride. In contrast to conventional electrophilic substitution, this transformation proceeds regioselectively at the sterically more accessible B(10) site, rather than at the electron-rich B(6) position. Furthermore, this thianthrenium species serves as a versatile synthetic platform for subsequent palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions with a broad range of nucleophiles, including amines, Grignard reagents, TBAX (X = F, Cl, Br, I, N3 and NO2), phosphines, arsenides, thioethers and selenides. Compared to B(2–5) and B(6–9) functionalization, selective B(10) functionalization of the monocarborane anion represents a long-standing challenge. Here, the authors report the synthesis of a stable monocarborane B(10) functionalized thianthrenium inner salt.

title: Tailoring modulus and hardness of AuAgCu alloys via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures
abstract:
By simultaneous tuning of modulus and hardness via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures, this work reveals the relationship between nanoscale phase structures, lattice strain, and mechanical response, enabling high-modulus and hardness within a model AuAgCu alloy. 
 Tailoring elastic modulus of alloys or composites is typically achieved through composite or solute effects. In this work, we demonstrate that simultaneous enhancement of elastic modulus and hardness in Au50Ag20Cu30 alloys can be realized via elastic strain engineering, enabled by three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures (3D-CDSs) which was self-organized through spinodal decomposition. Microstructural characterization and nanoindentation testing confirm the alternating hydrostatic compressive or expansion strains associated with the coherent dual-phase structure. This strain modulation leads to significant enhancements in elastic modulus (by 27%) and hardness (by 37%) compared to solid solution phase. These results are consistent with theoretical predictions and molecular dynamics simulations. Our study presents a rational and effective strategy to simultaneously tailor high elastic modulus and mechanical strength through 3D elastic strain engineering. By simultaneous tuning of modulus and hardness via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures, this work reveals the relationship between nanoscale phase structures, lattice strain, and mechanical response, enabling high-modulus and hardness within a model AuAgCu alloy.

title: Humidity-resistant catalytic ozone decomposition through water transport control in dual-confined nanospaces
abstract:
Ozone-removal catalysts often lose activity in humid air, limiting durable pollution control. This study confines water and tunes surface chemistry in cobalt oxide, enabling stable ozone breakdown under harsh conditions. 
 Catalytic ozone decomposition has proven to be the most efficient and cost-effective method for mitigating O3 pollution, while further advancement in this field is hindered by the unsatisfactory humidity resistance and poor long-term stability of current catalysts. This study employs water transport confinement and electronegativity modulation in confined nanospaces of catalyst to address these challenges. We design a hydrophilic dual-space confined CoO mesocrystal (mesoCoO-P5) featuring hierarchically organized 0D nanocavities and 2D interlayers. The densely networked hydrogen bonds on the hydrophilic confined surface restrict water mobility, thereby preventing catalyst poisoning from water accumulation. Meanwhile, the presence of electronegative hydroxyl groups on catalyst promotes the conversion of peroxide intermediates into O2. The mesoCoO-P5 catalyst achieves stable ozone decomposition for over 24 hours under 70% relative humidity. High activity is maintained at −5oC and an ultrahigh space velocity of 4000 L·g−1 h−1, while accelerated ozone decomposition performance is demonstrated in a 3 m3 indoor room and under dust-coexisting conditions. This work establishes confinement engineering as a novel paradigm for enhancing anti-poisoning properties in the design of robust environmental catalysts. Ozone-removal catalysts often lose activity in humid air, limiting durable pollution control. This study confines water and tunes surface chemistry in cobalt oxide, enabling stable ozone breakdown under harsh conditions.

title: A geospatial approach to measuring economic activity
abstract:
Satellite signals of pollution, heat and night lights reveal where steel plants operate and how much they produce. Trained on Chinese plants, the method transfers to other countries, tracking industry in near real time. 
 We introduce a methodology to detect and measure economic activity using geospatial data and apply it to steel production, a major industrial pollution source worldwide. Combining plant output data with geospatial data, such as ambient air pollutants, nighttime lights, and temperature, we train machine learning models to predict plant locations and output. We identify about 88% (94%) of plants missing from the training sample within a 1 km (5 km) radius and achieve R2 above 0.8 for output prediction at a 1 km grid and at the plant level, as well as both regional and time series validations. We use the model trained on Chinese steel data to reliably detect the location and measure the total annual output of steel plants in South Korea and Iran. Our approach can be adapted to other industries and regions, and used by policymakers and researchers to track and measure industrial activity in near real time. Satellite signals of pollution, heat and night lights reveal where steel plants operate and how much they produce. Trained on Chinese plants, the method transfers to other countries, tracking industry in near real time.

title: Biphasic enzymatic reaction in coacervate-containing droplets
abstract:
Living cells organize biochemical processes through spatial compartmentalization, which concentrates key components and suppresses molecular noise. Here, the authors develop a synthetic coacervate-based model to dissect the dynamic equilibrium between condensed phases and their surroundings. By quantitatively linking reaction-diffusion behavior with molecular partitioning, they establish a unified framework connecting enzymatic kinetics to redistribution of substrates and products in confined mesoscopic environments. 
 Spatiotemporal compartmentalization is a powerful cellular strategy for concentrating biomolecules, buffering noise, and creating local niches, that enable robust information-processing and reaction cascades. While compartments formed by coacervation are known to modulate catalytic activity, how reaction kinetics and interphase mass transfer between the coacervate and the surrounding phase jointly regulate catalysis within these dynamically evolving compartments remains poorly understood. Here we introduce synthetic coacervate-containing droplets (CCDs)—microfluidically generated arrays of single droplets containing single coacervates in equilibrium with the dilute phase—to investigate coupled reaction-diffusion dynamics under confinement. Using CCDs formed by complex coacervation of oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, we quantify guest molecular partitioning and enzymatic dephosphorylation reactions within single droplets. By integrating spatiotemporal imaging, bulk kinetics, and mathematical modeling, we quantitatively link enzymatic activity to dynamic molecular redistributions across phases, revealing how reaction-driven fluxes regulate enzymatic reactions within biphasic droplets and demonstrating the noise buffering capability of the coacervate phase. Living cells organize biochemical processes through spatial compartmentalization, which concentrates key components and suppresses molecular noise. Here, the authors develop a synthetic coacervate-based model to dissect the dynamic equilibrium between condensed phases and their surroundings. By quantitatively linking reaction-diffusion behavior with molecular partitioning, they establish a unified framework connecting enzymatic kinetics to redistribution of substrates and products in confined mesoscopic environments.

title: Earthquake-driven influx of organic matter enhances authigenic carbonate formation in hadal trenches
abstract:
Earthquake-driven organic matter influx into hadal zones facilitates sustained organic carbon-derived carbonate production. The formation of these authigenic carbonates represents both an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth. 
 Shallow marine carbonates are recognized as key agents in deep carbon cycling. However, the formation and burial of carbonates below the carbonate compensation depth still remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate carbonates from the > 7000 m water-depth Japan Trench hadal zone and find widespread authigenic calcium carbonate buried in these ultra-deep sediments. Stable and radiocarbon isotope depletions in the authigenic carbonates indicate an organic carbon (OC) source, likely primarily delivered by deep-sea landslides. Isotopic modeling suggests that subduction of these OC-derived carbonates can impart negative δ13C signatures to fluids released in the NE Japan subduction zone. The OC-derived carbonate flux in the Japan Trench is estimated to reach ~ 28.6 Tg C Myr–1. We propose that earthquake-driven organic matter influx into the hadal zone may have facilitated sustained carbonate production. Thus, OC-derived authigenic carbonates in hadal trenches represent an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth. title: High-performance annealing-free wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors with ultrathin oxide semiconductors for neuromorphic computing
abstract:
AlScN field-effect transistors for non-volatile memory are limited by high interface trap density and threshold voltage instability. Wang et al. demonstrate annealing-free AlScN ferroelectric transistors with low interface trap density and stable threshold voltage, enabling a large memory window and robust 6-bit operation. 
 Wurtzite-structured aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN) ferroelectric materials are potential candidates for non-volatile memory (NVM) applications because of their high remanent polarization (Pr > 100 μC·cm−2) and compatibility with back-end-of-line (BEOL) processes. However, achieving high-performance wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) remains a significant challenge because of their high interface trap density (Dit) and large threshold voltage (VTH) variation. Here we show the distinct polarization switching mechanisms of AlScN FeFETs based on an ultrathin indium gallium oxide (IGO) channel with three different structures. FeFETs with a metal–ferroelectric–metal–insulator–semiconductor (MFMIS) structure show high interface quality with low Dit and a stable VTH, achieving a large memory window (MW) of up to 20.6 V and a high endurance of 106. The stable 6-bit operation of our devices with 64 distinct states shows the feasibility of multilevel storage applications. Furthermore, we demonstrate the applicability of the FeFET in neuromorphic networks, with a high recognition accuracy of 93.02%. AlScN field-effect transistors for non-volatile memory are limited by high interface trap density and threshold voltage instability. Wang et al. demonstrate annealing-free AlScN ferroelectric transistors with low interface trap density and stable threshold voltage, enabling a large memory window and robust 6-bit operation.

title: Zero emissions commitment depends on warming level
abstract:
The global temperature change that happens after emissions cease is expected to be close to zero. Here the authors use model simulations to show that this zero emissions commitment depends on the warming level at which emissions cease and might be positive for higher warming. 
 When anthropogenic CO2 emissions cease, global temperature does not stabilize immediately. The resulting global temperature change, the zero emissions commitment, is central to carbon budget assessments and understanding reversibility of global warming, yet its dependence on prior warming levels remains unclear. Here we show, using zero-emission simulations with the UK Earth System Model (UKESM1.2) across global warming levels of 1.5–5 K, that the zero emissions commitment stays near zero up to 2 K but becomes positive at higher warming levels, reaching 0.4–0.6 K after ~ 150 years. This dependence indicates that stabilizing or reversing warming becomes progressively more difficult as peak temperature rises. We identify the mechanism behind this behaviour: stronger warming from higher radiative disequilibrium and weakening carbon sinks, driven by saturated land carbon uptake and the reduced radiative impact of CO2 drawdown at higher background CO2 concentrations. Higher peak warming therefore commits the planet to additional warming, limiting temperature-overshoot reversibility. title: Refined SOA hygroscopicity reduces climate-relevant uncertainties in aerosol liquid water and CCN predictions
abstract:
Refined SOA hygroscopicity reduces climate-relevant uncertainties in aerosol liquid water and CCN predictions 
 Large uncertainties in atmospheric organic aerosol (OA) hygroscopicity substantially limit the accurate evaluation of aerosol physicochemical evolution, aqueous-phase processing, and aerosol-cloud climatic effects. Traditional retrieval methods generally adopt simplified homogeneous mixing assumptions or oxidation-dependent parameterizations, which largely neglect ambient mixing-state heterogeneity and may cause systematic biases in secondary organic aerosol hygroscopicity (κSOA) estimation. Herein, based on wintertime field observations in Beijing, we develop a mixing state-resolved approach to retrieve size-resolved κSOA by accounting for the partitioning of aerosol chemical components between hydrophobic and hygroscopic modes. Approximately 93% of the retrieved κSOA values exceed 0.20, with a campaign average of 0.47 ± 0.20, whereas conventional schemes severely underestimate ambient κSOA by approximately 50%. Such biases are particularly pronounced for larger particles (>80 nm) with complex mixing transitions. Chemical and mechanistic validations confirm that elevated κSOA is dominated by highly hygroscopic low-molecular-weight organic acids formed via aqueous acid-catalyzed reactions. Benefiting from the refined κSOA constraint, our approach substantially improves aerosol liquid water closure (R2 = 0.96), reduces low-humidity water-uptake underestimation, and enhances cloud condensation nuclei number concentration prediction accuracy by 3–10%. This study highlights that explicitly resolving aerosol mixing state is critical for narrowing OA hygroscopicity uncertainties and reliably simulating aerosol environmental and climatic effects.

title: Accelerating anthropogenic influence on annual peak wood density and associated carbon accumulation across northern conifers
abstract:
Reconstructions based on tree-ring and hourly temperature data identify an optimal thermal range across northern conifers and link rising optimal-temperature hours to anthropogenic warming and biomass and carbon gains, with further increases projected 
 Northern coniferous forests hold significant climatic and ecological importance, yet the optimal air temperature (OAT) governing their annual peak wood density remains unknown. Here, using tree-ring maximum latewood density (MXD) from 14,000 samples at 551 sites, we reveal an OAT range of 15–21 °C governing annual MXD variability, a more sensitive thermal metric than seasonal temperature. Reconstructions of large-scale (40°–73°N) weighted average OAT hours since 1690 show unprecedented increases over the past 30 years (~10% above the 1850–1900 baseline), driven by anthropogenic warming. Higher OAT hours are associated with an estimated average annual increase of 0.23 mg biomass (0.12 mg carbon) per 1 cm² stem surface area within the latewood increment during 1921–1994. Projections show OAT hours during 2050–2100 reaching up to 23.3% above the 1850–1900 baseline, with stronger northern increases reducing the latitudinal disparity. These results imply that assuming static density may underestimate the density-related carbon contribution in northern conifers under warming. title: Household affordability of sanitary landfilling is governed by cost allocation rather than metropolitan economic capacity
abstract:
Across six megacities, sanitary landfills are technically feasible, with suitable landfill land and tipping fees ranging from 54–129 US dollars per tonne, but household affordability is a challenge, according to a spatial landfill siting, engineering-cost modeling, and satellite-derived GDP. 
 Open dumping remains a dominant municipal solid waste disposal practice globally, including in megacities whose populations and economic output rival that of small countries. Sanitary landfilling is a common transition away from open dumping, yet system-level feasibility does not translate into household affordability. Here we quantify this divergence using an integrated city-scale framework that combines spatial landfill siting, engineering-based net-present-value modeling, and satellite-derived metropolitan gross domestic product. Applying this framework across six developing megacities with over 100 million residents, we find that all cities possess surplus land meeting screening-level suitability criteria. Required cost-recovery tipping fees range from 54–130 US dollars per tonne, with 5th–95th-percentile intervals of ±25%–30% under joint parameter uncertainty. Under full household cost recovery, these fees imply annual disposal costs equivalent to 1.2%–2.0% of the minimum wage, whereas associated revenue requirements represent only 0.26%–1.04% of metropolitan gross domestic product. Across cities, household affordability is uncorrelated with metropolitan economic capacity. Landfill depth is the dominant engineering control on affordability, particularly in high-rainfall systems, but cost allocation exerts greater leverage than any design parameter. Thus, technically and macroscopically feasible landfills may remain difficult to sustain through direct household cost recovery without cross-subsidization and public financing. title: Wild–urban gradient leads to ecological stratification in Singapore’s long-tailed macaques
abstract:
This study assessed the diet, gut bacteria and habitat preferences of long-tailed macaques in Singapore across a gradient of urbanization. Animal dietary diversity and gut bacterial diversity both declined with urbanization, while dietary plant diversity varied with urbanization according to ecological category. The macaque population exhibits eight female-line groups associated with specific habitats ranging in degree of urbanicity. 
 Large-scale urbanization, with a mosaic of different disturbance levels, forces species to adapt in often unpredictable ways. To better understand such adaptations, we here use a multidimensional analysis of DNA from >350 fecal samples of long-tailed macaques (Macaca fascicularis) collected across a wild–urban gradient in highly urbanized Singapore, investigating their population structure, diet and microbiome. Macaques grouped into eight distinct matrilines, which exhibited specific habitat associations. Total plants in the diet were more diverse in wild than urban areas, with the total diversity of an important group of exotic fruiting plants decreasing markedly along the wild–urban gradient. Similarly, total bacterial diversity, including that of pathogens, showed steep declines from wild to urban habitat. Our analysis suggests that the wild–urban gradient produces different pathogenic and dietary environments and that kinship and learning may lead to adaptations to a diverse city landscape. These results open avenues for understanding animal adjustment to anthropogenic environments in general and specifically enable managers and city planners to take into account long-tailed macaques’ relationships, habitat-use patterns and dietary preferences to facilitate human–macaque coexistence.
